chat_response.message: The governed workflow recommends **decrease**. A modest price decrease is supported because claims performance was slightly better than baseline, with loss ratio moving from 71.8% to 71.1%, while commercial performance softened materially: quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 19.0% and renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 74.0% [claims-north_west-2025-12-01, conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01]. External market signals were also softer, with tracked competitors showing average price-index movement of -5.0%, and specialist market evidence stated that competitor price reductions coincided with stronger price sensitivity in broker and customer signals [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-market-retention, doc-broker-retention, doc-feedback-retention-1, doc-feedback-retention-2]. Pricing history adds caution on further firmness because a previous +2.0% action was associated with materially softer retention in following months [pricing-history-2024-06-01]. This is decision support only and needs an analyst’s explicit confirmation before any action is recorded.

specialist_reports.summary: For the period 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-01, claims performance was modestly better than baseline across the main measures. Claim frequency was 0.084 versus a baseline of 0.0844, a movement of -0.55%. Average severity was £1,606.8646 versus £1,615.2992, a movement of -0.52%. Incurred loss was £674,006.1067 versus £682,120.0492, a movement of -1.19%. Loss ratio was 0.7107 versus 0.7183, a movement of -1.06%. Overall, lower claim frequency and lower average severity coincided with lower incurred loss, and the period was associated with a slightly improved loss ratio relative to baseline.

For the period 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-01, quote-to-sale conversion moved from 0.2185 to 0.1896, a change of -13.24%. Renewal retention moved from 0.8797 to 0.7405, a change of -15.83%. Average quoted premium was broadly flat, moving from £621.5842 to £620.9067, or -0.11%.

The main pattern is that weaker conversion and weaker retention coincided with almost no movement in average quoted premium, so the portfolio’s softer outcomes were associated with factors other than any material change in quoted price level.

By segment, new business was essentially stable, moving from 0.1499 to 0.1498, or -0.06%. The more material movement was in the renewal segment, which moved from 0.2185 to 0.1896, or -13.24%. This indicates the deterioration was concentrated in renewal rather than new business.

Fictional competitor pricing moved down across the portfolio period while competitor price-position ranks were unchanged. Northgate Cover remained rank 1 with a price index movement of -4.89%, Meridian Insure remained rank 2 with a movement of -5.12%, and Bracken Mutual remained rank 3 with a movement of -5.06%. This is consistent with retrieved market reporting that said these fictional competitors reduced personal motor renewal pricing by roughly 4% to 6% over the past quarter, indicating a softer competitive backdrop for any further increase. Broker notes said renewal shopping-around behaviour had risen following the previous portfolio-level increase, and brokers flagged retention risk if pricing firms further. Customer feedback also showed price as the dominant renewal theme across November and December, with repeated price-related comments rather than a one-off spike. Repair-cost intelligence was broadly in line with historical norms and did not show a clear signal in either direction for claims severity. Overall, competitor price reductions coincided with stronger price sensitivity in broker and customer signals, while cost intelligence was stable rather than supportive of firmer pricing.

On 2024-06-01, the portfolio took a 2.0% renewal price increase. In the recorded history, this action was associated with conversion moving down 8.0% and loss ratio improving by 0.5%. The recorded rationale notes that retention softened materially in the following months. [pricing-history-2024-06-01]

recommendation.rationale: A modest price decrease is supported because claims performance was slightly better than baseline, with loss ratio moving from 71.8% to 71.1%, while commercial performance softened materially: quote-to-sale conversion moved from 21.9% to 19.0% and renewal retention moved from 88.0% to 74.0% [claims-north_west-2025-12-01, conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01]. External market signals were also softer, with tracked competitors showing average price-index movement of -5.0%, and specialist market evidence stated that competitor price reductions coincided with stronger price sensitivity in broker and customer signals [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-market-retention, doc-broker-retention, doc-feedback-retention-1, doc-feedback-retention-2]. Pricing history adds caution on further firmness because a previous +2.0% action was associated with materially softer retention in following months [pricing-history-2024-06-01].
counter_evidence: Claims performance was somewhat favorable versus baseline, with loss ratio moving from 71.8% to 71.1%, which does not create strong urgency for a larger price decrease [claims-north_west-2025-12-01].

Repair-cost intelligence was described as broadly in line with historical norms and did not show a clear signal in either direction for claims severity, so cost evidence is neutral rather than strongly supportive of repricing [doc-repair-cost-retention].

Competitor price-position ranks were described as unchanged, so the evidence indicates softer market pricing but not worsening relative rank position within the tracked set [competitors-north_west-2025-12-01].

The specialist conversion summary said average quoted premium was broadly flat, so weaker conversion and retention were associated with factors other than any material change in quoted price level; that means a price reduction may not fully address the softer outcomes on its own [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01, retention-north_west-2025-12-01].
conditions: Keep any analyst-selected action within the stated policy limit of +/-5%.

If a decrease is considered, keep it modest and targeted within -2.0% to 0.0% given only slight claims improvement and neutral repair-cost signals [claims-north_west-2025-12-01, doc-repair-cost-retention].
Review renewal-focused execution first, because the specialist conversion evidence said deterioration was concentrated in renewal rather than new business [conversion-north_west-2025-12-01].
Monitor retention and conversion closely after any analyst decision because prior +2.0% pricing history was associated with materially softer retention [pricing-history-2024-06-01].
Requires explicit approval from a qualified pricing analyst before any action; the copilot cannot execute a pricing change.
